items.stem: Define the term 'above-the-line promotion'.
items.answer: Promotion through independent mass media, such as television, radio, newspapers and billboards, aimed at a wide audience.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Promotion through independent mass media, such as television, radio, newspapers and billboards, aimed at a wide audience. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between above-the-line and below-the-line promotion.
items.answer: Above-the-line promotion uses mass media such as television and newspapers to reach a wide audience; below-the-line uses methods controlled by the business, such as sales promotions, direct mail and sponsorship, often aimed at specific customers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark above-the-line; 1 mark below-the-line; 1 mark example/contrast. [3]

items.stem: Explain two factors a business should consider when choosing a promotion method.
items.answer: The cost compared with the marketing budget; and the target market – the method must reach the customers the business wants, e.g. social media for young people.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark factor, 1 mark explanation): budget, target market, product type, competitors, stage of life cycle. [4]

items.stem: Desert Bloom is a public limited company in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates with about 3,100 staff. It operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels. Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Explain the promotion methods Desert Bloom could use to launch serviced apartments for long-stay guests.
items.answer: Points to develop for Desert Bloom: promotion informs and persuades customers; above-the-line advertising for awareness; below-the-line offers to encourage trial; methods must suit the target market and budget.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: promotion informs and persuades customers. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Desert Bloom (hospitality). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. above-the-line advertising for awareness; below-the-line offers to encourage trial. [3]

items.stem: Based in Pune, Green Valley Dairy Co-operative (co-operative) collects milk from 900 member farmers and makes yoghurt and cheese. The business has around 80 employees. The members are arguing about how much of the profit to reinvest. Explain the benefits to Green Valley Dairy of below-the-line promotion.
items.answer: Points to develop for Green Valley Dairy: below-the-line methods are controlled by the business; targeted at specific customers; often cheaper than mass media; easier to measure results.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: below-the-line methods are controlled by the business. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Green Valley Dairy (agriculture and food processing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. targeted at specific customers; often cheaper than mass media. [3]

items.stem: Café Cordillera SAS is a private limited company based in Bogotá, Colombia. It roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés and employs about 900 people. The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Evaluate the most effective promotion methods for Café Cordillera.
items.answer: For: mass media for awareness; sales promotions for trial; personal selling for business customers. Against: cost; target market fit; short-term effects. Judgement: for Café Cordillera it depends mainly on the budget, and also on the target customers.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Café Cordillera: food and drink retail, about 900 employees, private limited company in Colombia; the owners want to double the number of cafés within three years). AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the budget; the target customers; the stage of the product life cycle. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Café Cordillera. [10]

items.stem: Define the term 'digital marketing'.
items.answer: Promoting products through digital channels such as websites, search engines, email, apps and social media.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Promoting products through digital channels such as websites, search engines, email, apps and social media. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two advantages of digital marketing for a small business.
items.answer: It is cheaper than mass media, so a small budget can still reach customers; and it can be targeted at specific groups and the results measured, for example clicks and sales.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain one disadvantage of using social media to promote a product.
items.answer: Negative comments or poor reviews spread quickly and can damage the brand, and it needs staff time to monitor and respond.
items.markingKey: 1 mark disadvantage; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Savanna Fresh is a private limited company in Nairobi, Kenya with about 850 staff. It grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe. items.answer: Points to develop for Savanna Fresh: social media marketing engages customers online; negative reviews spread quickly; changes to platform rules or costs; not all customers use social media.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: social media marketing engages customers online. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Savanna Fresh (horticulture). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. negative reviews spread quickly; changes to platform rules or costs. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'distribution channel'.
items.answer: The route a product takes from the producer to the final consumer, for example through wholesalers and retailers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The route a product takes from the producer to the final consumer, for example through wholesalers and retailers. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two factors that affect the choice of distribution channel.
items.answer: The type of product: perishable or technical products need short channels; and the target market: customers spread over a wide area may require wholesalers or online sales.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark factor, 1 mark explanation): product type, cost, control, target market, competitors' channels. [4]

items.stem: Explain why many businesses now sell through both shops and online channels.
items.answer: Online sales reach more customers at any time and lower costs, while shops let customers see products and get advice; using both meets different preferences and increases sales.
items.markingKey: 1 mark online benefit; 1 mark shop benefit; 1 mark combined effect. [3]

items.answer: Points to develop for Cape Brew: channels differ in number of intermediaries; product characteristics; location of target customers; cost and control.

items.stem: Define the term 'marketing mix'.
items.answer: The combination of decisions about product, price, promotion and place used to market a product.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The combination of decisions about product, price, promotion and place used to market a product. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why the elements of the marketing mix must be integrated.
items.answer: If they are inconsistent – for example a luxury product sold at a low price in discount shops – customers receive mixed messages and the brand image is damaged.
items.markingKey: 1 mark consistency; 1 mark example of inconsistency and effect. [2]

items.stem: Explain why "people" is an important element of the marketing mix for a service business.
items.answer: Services are delivered by employees, so their skills, attitude and appearance determine the customer's experience and whether they return.
items.markingKey: 1 mark staff deliver the service; 1 mark effect on customer experience/loyalty. [2]
